guide_line: Balance an equation, label each state, and cancel spectator ions to leave the net ionic equation.
steps: Write the correct formulas first. Change coefficients, never subscripts, to balance.
Count atoms of one element at a time. Match metals and other elements that appear once on each side before H and O.
State symbols sit in parentheses and are not coefficients: (s) solid, (l) liquid, (g) gas, (aq) dissolved in water.
A molecular equation shows whole formulas. A complete ionic equation splits each dissolved salt into ions and still shows the spectators.
Ions that stay dissolved on both sides are spectators. Cross them out. What remains is the net ionic equation.

worked_example.q: Balance C2H6 + O2 -> CO2 + H2O. Give the coefficients in order, separated by commas.
steps: One ethane has 2 C and 6 H, so the carbon dioxide coefficient is 2 and the water coefficient is 3.
That puts 4 + 3 = 7 oxygen atoms on the right, which is not a whole number of O2.
Double every coefficient: 2 C2H6 + 7 O2 -> 4 CO2 + 6 H2O. Carbon, hydrogen, and oxygen now match.

similar_problem.q: Balance C3H8 + O2 -> CO2 + H2O. Give the coefficients in order, separated by commas.
similar_problem.hint: Balance the three carbon atoms and the eight hydrogen atoms before you touch oxygen.

problems.q: Balance C2H6 + O2 -> CO2 + H2O. Give the smallest whole-number coefficients in order, separated by commas.
problems.why: C2H6 gives 2 CO2 and 3 H2O, but that needs 7/2 O2. Multiply through by 2: 2 C2H6 + 7 O2 -> 4 CO2 + 6 H2O.
hints: Two C2H6 give 4 CO2 and 6 H2O. The oxygen atoms on the right then total 14, so the O2 coefficient is 7.

problems.q: Balance C3H8 + O2 -> CO2 + H2O. Give the smallest whole-number coefficients in order, separated by commas.
problems.why: Propane has 3 C and 8 H, so the products are 3 CO2 and 4 H2O. The right side then has 10 oxygen atoms, which is 5 O2. Coefficients: 1, 5, 3, 4.
hints: One propane makes 3 CO2 and 4 H2O. That is 6 + 4 = 10 oxygen atoms, so the O2 coefficient is 5.

guided.prompt: How many CO2 molecules balance the 3 carbon atoms in C3H8?
guided.hint: One CO2 holds one carbon, so the CO2 coefficient is 3.

guided.prompt: How many H2O molecules balance the 8 hydrogen atoms?
guided.hint: Each water holds 2 H, so 8 H needs 4 H2O.

guided.prompt: How many O2 molecules supply the oxygen in 3 CO2 and 4 H2O?
guided.hint: The products hold 10 oxygen atoms, which is 5 O2.

guided.prompt: Write the four coefficients in order, separated by commas.
guided.hint: The order is C3H8, O2, CO2, H2O.

problems.q: Balance N2 + H2 -> NH3. Give the smallest whole-number coefficients in order, separated by commas.
problems.why: N2 already supplies two N atoms, so the ammonia coefficient is 2. Two NH3 hold six H atoms, so the H2 coefficient is 3. Coefficients: 1, 3, 2.
hints: Nitrogen is already matched. Six hydrogen atoms in two ammonia molecules need three H2.

problems.q: Balance Fe2O3 + CO -> Fe + CO2. Give the smallest whole-number coefficients in order, separated by commas.
problems.why: Fe2O3 has two Fe atoms, so the iron metal coefficient is 2. It also has three O atoms, and each CO takes one O to become CO2, so both CO and CO2 get coefficient 3. Coefficients: 1, 3, 2, 3.
hints: One Fe2O3 holds three oxygen atoms, and each CO takes one of them to become CO2.

problems.q: Balance C4H10 + O2 -> CO2 + H2O. Give the smallest whole-number coefficients in order, separated by commas.
problems.why: Use 2 C4H10 so the hydrogen count is even for whole O2. That makes 8 CO2 and 10 H2O. Oxygen atoms on the right: 16 + 10 = 26, so 13 O2. Coefficients: 2, 13, 8, 10.
hints: Start from 2 C4H10 so the 20 hydrogen atoms make 10 water molecules, then count the oxygen atoms.

problems.q: Balance Al + HCl -> AlCl3 + H2. Give the smallest whole-number coefficients in order, separated by commas.
problems.why: AlCl3 takes Cl in threes and H2 takes H in twos, so use 6 HCl. That makes 2 AlCl3 and 3 H2, and the Al coefficient is 2. Coefficients: 2, 6, 2, 3.
hints: AlCl3 needs chlorine in threes and H2 needs hydrogen in twos, so the HCl coefficient to try is 6.

problems.q: Solid potassium chlorate, KClO3, decomposes to solid KCl and O2 gas. Write the balanced equation using -> between reactants and products.
problems.why: K and Cl are already 1 to 1. Oxygen is 3 on the left and 2 on the right, so use 2 KClO3 and 3 O2: 2 KClO3 -> 2 KCl + 3 O2.
hints: Do not change the subscripts. Two KClO3 hold six oxygen atoms, which is three O2.

problems.q: Aqueous silver nitrate is mixed with aqueous sodium chloride, and solid silver chloride forms. Write the net ionic equation. Use -> and write ions as Ag+ and Cl-.
problems.why: AgNO3 and NaCl split into ions. Na+ and NO3- stay dissolved, so they cancel. The net ionic equation is Ag+ + Cl- -> AgCl.
hints: Na+ and NO3- are aqueous on both sides, so only Ag+ and Cl- stay in the net ionic equation.

problems.q: Aqueous barium chloride is mixed with aqueous sodium sulfate, and solid barium sulfate forms. List the spectator ions.
problems.why: Ba2+ and SO42- form solid BaSO4. Na+ and Cl- remain in the solution, so those two are the spectators.
hints: Ba2+ and SO42- are locked in the solid BaSO4. The ions still dissolved are the spectators.

problems.q: Aqueous HCl is mixed with aqueous NaOH. Write the net ionic equation. Use H+, OH-, and ->.
problems.why: Both reactants are strong, so they are ions in water. Na+ and Cl- cancel. What remains is H+ + OH- -> H2O.
hints: Na+ and Cl- appear on both sides and cancel. H+ and OH- are what make the water.

problems.q: Zinc metal is placed in aqueous copper(II) sulfate, and copper metal forms. Write the net ionic equation. Use Cu2+, Zn2+, and ->.
problems.why: Sulfate stays dissolved, so it is a spectator. Zinc metal gives electrons to Cu2+. The net ionic equation is Zn + Cu2+ -> Zn2+ + Cu.
hints: Sulfate is aqueous before and after the reaction, so cancel it and keep the zinc and copper.

problems.q: A substance dissolved in water is labeled with which state symbol? Include the parentheses.
problems.why: (aq) means aqueous, dissolved in water. (s), (l), and (g) are the pure solid, liquid, and gas.
hints: The four state symbols are (s), (l), (g), and (aq). Dissolved in water is the one that is not a pure solid, liquid, or gas.

problems.q: Oxygen as a pure gas is written O2 followed by which state symbol? Include the parentheses.
problems.why: A pure gas uses (g). (aq) would mean the oxygen is dissolved in water.
hints: Oxygen that is not dissolved is a pure gas. Use the state symbol for a gas, not the symbol for a water solution.

problems.q: Aqueous sodium chloride is mixed with aqueous silver nitrate, and solid AgCl forms. Write the complete ionic equation, spectators included, in this order: Na+, Cl-, Ag+, NO3- on the left and Na+, NO3-, AgCl on the right. Use ->.
problems.a: Na+ + Cl- + Ag+ + NO3- -> Na+ + NO3- + AgCl
problems.why: NaCl and AgNO3 are dissolved, so they split. AgCl is the solid, so it stays together. The complete ionic equation still shows Na+ and NO3-.
hints: Split NaCl into Na+ and Cl- and AgNO3 into Ag+ and NO3-. AgCl stays together because it is the solid.

check.text: Na+ + Cl- + Ag+ + NO3- -> Na+ + NO3- + AgCl
answers: Na+ + Cl- + Ag+ + NO3- → Na+ + NO3- + AgCl
